metadata.rules_text:
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≥15 days), model tends to overestimate prices; apply downward bias correction, especially after spikes.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >15% from prior 5-day avg), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast by 5–10% in next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment flips from negative to positive (or vice versa) within 3–5 days, model lags in adjusting; align forecast with sentiment shift by +2–5% in next 2–4 days.
- Mean reversion is strong in 3–7 day horizons; if forecast is >10% above recent 7-day avg, reduce by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.
- In 30-day horizon, model often underestimates downward trends; add 3–5% buffer for negative sentiment + low volume signals.
- If sentiment history shows 3+ consecutive negative days, model tends to overcorrect upward; cap forecast at 10% above recent 5-day high.
